findings.title: Login-cache invalidation uses wrapped isEnabled and skips real membership changes
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate treats the pre-update model from getById as the source of truth for whether the IdP is a login IdP. With the organization feature on, getById returns a wrapper whose isEnabled() is false whenever the linked organization is missing, disabled, or the organization provider is disabled, even if the stored IdP is enabled. LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate uses that isEnabled(). The getForLogin cache, however, is filled from the JPA query, which only checks the IdP's own enabled, link-only, hide-on-login, and broker-public flags. If the org is disabled (so the wrapped original already fails the predicate) and the update also fails the predicate — for example hide-on-login or link-only is set, broker-public is cleared, or the IdP enabled flag is turned off — both sides fail and the method returns without invalidating the login list caches. Those lists still contain the IdP. After the organization is enabled again, getById shows the updated flags, but OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), not hide-on-login or link-only, so a hidden or link-only broker can be offered on the login page until the cache expires.

findings.title: getForLogin cache drops result order
findings.body: Cached login results are stored in a Set of internal ids and returned from a HashSet. The previous getForLogin implementation returned the delegate stream order (stable storage order, typically alias or guiOrder). HashSet iteration order is undefined and can change between calls even when the membership is unchanged. Callers that do not sort, unlike OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean, will show identity-provider buttons in a shuffling order.

findings.title: Login-cache test cleanup deletes the wrong IdP alias
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup with testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove (also at the hide-on-login provider created later in the same test). The providers are actually created as idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-20, so cleanup issues DELETE for a non-existent alias "alias" and leaves every created broker in the shared test realm. Later tests that count identity providers, including testCacheIDPByOrg's expectation of 6 providers for an organization, can fail or become order-dependent, and the new test does not isolate its data.
